card_b.headline: SUBEXPONENTIAL IS NOT POLYNOMIAL
card_b.sub_line: Exact counting · fixed-width SAT · polynomial space

script:
OpenAI has posted a preprint claiming to overturn a decades-old assumption in computer science.
The Exponential Time Hypothesis says that solving three sat, in the worst case, requires time exponential in the number of variables.
The paper claims something stronger than finding one solution: computing the exact number of satisfying assignments for fixed-width Boolean formulas, using subexponential time and polynomial space.
The approach translates Boolean constraints into algebra, then reuses shared linear summaries instead of expanding every possible assignment.
But subexponential does not mean polynomial. An asymptotic improvement does not automatically make enormous problems practical.
This does not prove that P equals N P, or that every encryption system is suddenly broken.
The claim challenges assumptions behind many conditional hardness bounds. The story is a proposed new route around a computational wall, with important limits to understand.
Watch the full explainer on The Classical Remix.
